compliance.certifications: BSMI, CE, KCC, NRTL, RCM, UKCA, VCCI, TEC, ANATEL, ICASA (data sheet)

environmental.humidity: 5 to 90 percent non-condensing (guide Table 2); the data sheet says 5 to 95 percent
environmental.storage-temp: -25 to 70 C (guide Table 2); the data sheet says -40 to 70 C

features.optics-qsfp28: 100G, 50G, 40G, 25G and 10G with breakout, in the 96 QSFP cages (data sheet)

management.console: RJ-45 RS-232 serial on the front, 9600 baud 8N1, no flow control
management.oob: one 10/100/1000 management port on the front
management.usb: one USB port on the front, for software or configuration updates

performance.ports-max-speed: 96 ports of 100 Gbps; 192 of 50 Gbps; 96 of 40 Gbps; 192 of 25 or 10 Gbps

physical.size-over-ears: 48.3 x 8.8 x 76.1 cm (19 x 3.50 x 30.0 in) with the mounting ears (guide Table 1)
physical.weight: 23.6 kg (52.0 lbs) for the 7280CR3-96 and the 7280CR3K-96 (guide Table 1, data sheet)

power.power-measure: typical at 25 C ambient with 50 percent load on all ports (data sheet)

thermal.airflow: front-to-rear, set by the fan modules and supplies fitted

configs.description: The chassis with two AC supplies and four fan modules fitted, front-to-rear air, before any part number: the shape every build below starts from.
configs.name: base

configs.description: Two DC supplies and front-to-rear air: PWR-2411-DC-RED supplies and FAN-7012H-RED fan modules. The data sheet lists no DC part number for the switch; the supplies are spares, and a DC build is ordered through the "#" configurable SKUs.
configs.name: dc-f

configs.description: The 7280CR3-96 with two AC supplies and front-to-rear air: PWR-2411-AC-RED supplies and FAN-7012H-RED fan modules, all with red handles. Ordered as DCS-7280CR3-96-F.
configs.name: f

configs.description: The 7280CR3K-96, the same hardware with the large-routes licence, with front-to-rear air. Ordered as DCS-7280CR3K-96-F.
configs.name: k-f

gaps.note: The 7280CR3K-96 carries the large-routes licence (over 5M routes) where the 7280CR3-96 does not. No configuration can state a device attribute (the same open gap as cisco/asr-9001). The data sheet gives the two the same hardware figures.

Storage temperature -25 to 70 C (guide Table 2) against -40 to 70 C (data sheet), and relative humidity 5 to 90 percent against 5 to 95 percent. The guide's, the older document by three months, are in attrs.
gaps.wanted: the maker's statement of which is current.

gaps.note: The guide's chapter 3 figures are isometric drawings and carry no measure, and the kit guides for KIT-7202, KIT-2POST and KIT-7004-2UL are not held, so no ear position or rail kit is written.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned drawing of the mounting bracket position, and the kit guides.

gaps.note: Guide table 10 describes port LEDs near the ports and Figure C-8 draws no lamp whose count or place can be read. No port lamp is modelled.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the lit face, or a larger figure.

gaps.note: The speed strips' legends, the small print over the cages, the system and fan lamp glyphs and the PS1 and PS2 legends are unreadable or barely readable in the 552 px figure. The glyphs and the two PS legends are drawn as read; the strip and cage legends are not drawn.
Which side the latches of the stacked cages face is not visible in the figure. The library's belly-to-belly convention is used (upper cage upright, lower turned 180).
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the stacked cages.

gaps.note: The PWR-2411-DC supplies are the library's existing drawing of that module, an AC housing with a plain terminal block; the guide shows a DC supply only in isometric figures.
gaps.wanted: a flat drawing or photograph of the PWR-2411-DC.

gaps.note: The guide's power tables and the data sheet give whole-switch figures only; the fan modules' missing power figure (lint L27) stands. The supplies state their output.

gaps.wanted: a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor
`physical-context` on 6 bays (rear 6); `physical-context` on port group qsfp28 - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

chassis.note: Guide Table 1: 48.3 x 8.8 x 76.1 cm (19 x 3.50 x 30.0 in), 23.6 kg (52.0 lbs), the same for the 7280CR3-96 and the 7280CR3K-96. Data sheet: 43.99 x 8.79 x 76.1 cm (17.3 x 3.46 x 29.96 in), 52 lbs (23.6 kg). The width: 48.3 cm is over the mounting ears, so the body between them, which is what is modelled, is the data sheet's 43.99 cm (440.0 here), a 21.5 mm ear each side. The height is the data sheet's 87.9. The depth is the data sheet's 761.0. 2RU.

colour.note: The front plate is the 7280CR3-32D4's #aaabad, read there as the median of bare-plate pixels in the guide's figure of the same family.

configurations.note: Data sheet ordering information: DCS-7280CR3-96-F and DCS-7280CR3K-96-F ("front to rear air, 2 x AC"). The "#" SKUs ("configurable fans and psu") are orders of parts, not part numbers a DCIM can hold, and are not listed. The data sheet lists no DC build of the switch: the PWR-2411-DC-RED supply is a spare, so the DC configuration is an example with no part number. The K build shares the base model's size, weight, figure and supplies and differs in the large-routes licence, which a configuration cannot state; it is a configuration with its own part number. There is no empty-bay (-S) configuration: no -S suffix exists in this family and the guide draws no blank for a power supply or fan module. No rear-to-front build is listed.

ears.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide's chapter 3 mounts the 2RU switch with the accessory-kit brackets in isometric drawings that carry no measure. The data sheet lists the spares KIT-2POST, KIT-7202 and KIT-7004-2UL. No figure measures a bracket position, and the kit guides are not held, so no ear position is written and no rail kit is listed in chassis.kits. Recorded in the gap rack-ears.

environment.note: Guide Table 2: operating 0 to 40 C, storage -25 to 70 C, altitude 0 to 3,000 m, humidity 5 to 90 percent non-condensing. Data sheet: operating 0 to 40 C, storage -40 to 70 C, humidity 5 to 95 percent, altitude 0 to 3,000 m. Storage temperature and humidity differ: gap `environment`, the guide's used.

front-legend.note: The model legend reads "7280CR3-96" at the bottom left (read at 552 px; the print is small), under the maker's wordmark at the top left. THE WORDMARK IS NOT DRAWN: a logo-zone region is reserved over it and the plain model text is set. The text is as the guide's caption names the model.

front-ports.note: Figure C-8 at 1.2545 px/mm, read in an eight-times enlargement. Ninety-six QSFP100 cages in three rows. The top row is sixteen single cages (81 to 96) in blocks of two columns, the first centred 22.6 mm from the left, with 4.5 mm gaps between the pairs of columns (the tab centres of 81 and 82 read 22.6 and 41.0, of 83 at 63.9, of 96 at 331.0). Below it are two rows of ten blocks, each block two columns of two stacked cages (1 and 2 over 3 and 4): the tabs read 22.6 and 41.0 mm for the first block, 63.9 and 82.6 for the second, and 415.6 for port 39, so the column pitch is 19.0 (the registry's ganged-QSFP pitch) inside a block and 3.45 mm more between blocks, the same in all three rows. The rows read from the tabs at 10.1, 30.8, 46.6, 60.7 and 76.5 mm down for the top row and the four cage rows: the upper block's rows are 15.8 mm apart, the lower block's likewise, and the two blocks 14.1 mm apart. The belly-to-belly orientation of each stack is the library's convention (upper cage upright, lower turned 180); the figure is too small to show the latch side.

fru-bays.note: Guide Appendix E (E.2 power supplies, E.3 fan modules) gives removal and installation procedures, and the data sheet calls the supplies "1+1 hot-swappable" and the fans "hot-swap". SO THE TWO POWER SUPPLIES AND THE FOUR FAN MODULES ARE BAYS. Nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit. The management ports are part of the chassis and are placements on the front.

gate-1-front.note: Figure C-8 passes. The raster is 552 x 190 pixels; the chassis measures 552 px wide and 110 px tall (aspect 5.0), against the data sheet's 440.0 / 87.9 = 5.0, so the figure is orthographic and carries geometry at 1.2545 px/mm (the 440 mm body is the scale anchor, its left edge read at 1 px and its top at 37 px). One pixel is 0.8 mm, so every position is good to about 0.8 mm, and every one is `estimated` because it is read off a picture and no dimension states it. The cages were read from the white port-number tabs in an eight-times enlargement.

gate-1-rear.note: Figure D-3 is a 565 x 197 px raster whose chassis is 528 px between its edges and 106 px tall (aspect 4.98 against 5.0), 1.2 px/mm over the 440 mm body; it passes. The guide draws the rear generically (D-1 to D-4) and does not say which model uses which. The 7280CR3-96 is mapped to D-3 by its four fan modules (data sheet: "Hot-swappable Fans 4 (N+1 redundant)"), its 2RU height, its two power supplies and the guide's Table 6, which says the 2RU switches' grounding "location is on the back for those supporting direct attach" and lists the CR3-96 as "Attach directly". The positions are those the 7280DR3A-36 file measured off the same figure. THE MAPPING IS ESTIMATED.

interface-names.note: Not printed and not modelled. EOS names ports Ethernet1 to Ethernet96 and Management1; this is the vendor's convention and no held document prints it.

lifecycle.note: Searched 2026-10-23 (web searches of Arista's end-of-sale notices) for a notice for the 7280CR3-96 and 7280CR3K-96: none found. The notices the searches returned were for older 7280 models and for the 7280SR3K-48YC8 (notice 23789) and 7280CR3K-36S (notice 23790) series, not for this one.

management-ports.note: Figure C-8 callouts 6 to 8: the console port (serial, left), the USB port (middle) and the Ethernet management port (right), in a row at the top right on a grey strip printed with their symbols, 5.8 to 19.4 mm down. Placed as the library places the 7280DR3A-36's row, with the USB port upright. The symbols are a console box, a USB trident and a double arrow.

other-faces.note: No source draws the top, bottom or sides flat. The guide's installation figures are isometric. Each carries an `empty` sentence. Table 6 puts the 2RU grounding on the back (attach directly, right-angle lug recommended); the guide's figure 4-3 shows a side-attach adapter this model does not take.

port-lamps.note: NOT MODELLED. Guide Appendix A.1.2, Table 10 says port LEDs sit near their ports (off link down, green link up, yellow software disabled, flashing yellow failed diagnostics), but Figure C-8 draws no lamp a reader can count beside any cage. Recorded in the gap port-lamps.

port-numbering.note: Figure C-8 (callout 9, "Port numbers") prints 1 over 2 and 3 over 4 in each block and so on, 1 to 40 across the first block row and 41 to 80 across the second, and 81 to 96 left to right along the top row. The odd number is the upper cage. The figure prints each number on a white tab over the cage opening; a seated cage hides the tab, so the model prints the numerals in the band between the rows (the odd number left of its column centre and the even one right of it) and under the top row. EOS interface names are not printed on the metal and are not modelled.

power.note: Guide Table 4: typical / maximum 1003 W / 1803 W for the 7280CR3-96 and the 7280CR3K-96, each with PWR-2411-AC or PWR-2411-DC. The data sheet states the same figures with typical "measured at 25C ambient with 50% load on all ports".

rear.note: Figure D-3 at 1.2 px/mm, as the 7280DR3A-36 file reads it: four fan modules 79.6 mm wide and 81.5 mm tall at 5.9, 103.9, 189.4 and 274.9 mm across, a grounding strip 15.0 mm wide at 87.2 mm between the first and second fan with two ground screws and an earth symbol, and the two power supplies one above the other at 361.0 mm across (2.0 and 45.0 mm down, 73.5 mm wide, the data sheet's "73.5MM"). The guide's figure D-3 callout 7 names the "Earth grounding pad".

rear-fan.note: Data sheet: "Hot-swappable Fans 4 (N+1 redundant)", "Fan Tray FAN-7012H" and the spare FAN-7012H-RED (front-to-rear airflow); no reverse-airflow 2RU fan is listed and the airflow is "Front to rear". Guide section 2.1: a red handle is an air-exit module. The four fan modules are bays that accept the FAN-7012H-RED.

sources.note: 7280R3 Series Quick Start Guide, Arista Networks, document DOC-07041-01, 63 pages, PDF created 2025-05-16 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/qsg/qsg-books/QS_7280R3.pdf): Table 1 (dimensions and weights), Table 2 (operating and storage), Table 3 (power input), Table 4 (power draw and supported supplies), section 2.1 (airflow orientation, handle colour), Table 6 (grounding of the 2RU switches), section 4.5 (serial and management cables), Appendix A (status indicators, Tables 9 to 13), Appendix C (Figure C-8, the front panel of the DCS-7280CR3-96 and 7280CR3K-96), Appendix D (Figure D-3, the rear panel with ground attach point, 2RU), Appendix E (field replacement). 7280R3 Series Data Center Switch Router Data Sheet, Arista Networks, 03-0045-59, dated August 11th, 2025 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/Datasheets/7280R3-Data-Sheet.pdf): the model comparison of the 7280CR3-96 and 7280CR3K-96, the power supply specifications and the ordering information. The 2022 7280 1RU Gen 3 guide (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/qsg/qsg-books/QS_7280_1RU_Gen3.pdf) does not list this model, so Figure C-8 has no second reading. Held and checked first: intake COVERAGE.md and SOURCES.md, which list no photograph, Visio stencil, 3D model or CAD file for this model (Arista publishes none; the stencil zip could not be fetched). The data sheet's picture of the face is a thumbnail. No drawing, photograph or logo is copied into the library, only transcribed facts and new drawings.

speed-strips.note: Guide Figure C-8 callout 1, "Port speed groups": purple and blue strips above the top row and between the two block rows, with tiny legends. The strips are drawn in those colours; the legends are unreadable and are not drawn.

status-lamps.note: Guide Appendix A.1.1, Table 9 and Figure C-8 callouts 2 to 5: a system status lamp (blinking green on power-up, green normal, blue locator, amber for two or more failed fans), a fan status lamp (green, amber for one module removed or failed, red for two or more) and a status lamp for each of the two power supplies (green operating, off removed or faulty). Four lamps in a row at 356.6, 361.4, 366.3 and 371.3 mm and 18.6 mm down, on a small grey plate (353.9 to 374.5 mm across), with a symbol or legend above each: a circled mark, a fan, and two legends read as PS1 and PS2.

vents.note: The figure shows a grid of dark squares along the left edge, along the right edge and between the lamp plate and the top row, and a ribbed strip along the bottom lip. A dark hole sits at the lower left (5.2 mm across, 43.8 mm down). Each is drawn in its measured extent; the individual squares are not drawn one by one.
